newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: PHILIPS SAYS GRUNDIG REVAMP GOING TO PLAN.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPS SAYS GRUNDIG REVAMP GOING TO PLAN.

text.p: Philips Electronics said on Thursday that restructuring at its Grundig consumer products unit was proceeding as planned and it had no plans to divest the loss-making unit which, it said, should be back in profit by the end of next year.
"We expect Grundig to break into profit in the last quarter of 1997," finance director Dudley Eustace told a news conference.
"We're doing our best to get Grundig back to its proud self...we are not offering Grundig for sale," he told reporters.

Although Grundig had headed further into the red during the third quarter, it was not expected to deepen losses over the full 1996 year, Eustace said, adding the final 1995 quarter had been a very bad one for the German unit.

Philips said earlier that higher losses at Grundig had helped push income from operations in Consumer Products sector 10 million guilders into the red in the first nine months of 1996, compared with positive income of 287 million guilders in 1995.
Group third-quarter net from normal operations dropped to 123 million guilders, just over half the lowest analyst's estimate, and versus a previous 539 million guilders.
Analysts had forecast profits of 240-360 million guilders.
-- Lien van der Leij, Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000.
